title: An embedder deleting a message is not covered by the checkpoint
description:
Found while landing the write-ahead log (decision mimid-1wgh.134, commit 99ddbc9c).

The rewritten chat_delete test proves the agent's own deletion property: after a destroy and a `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`, a destroyed chat's text is in none of mimid.sqlite, -wal or -shm. Nothing checkpoints on the delete path, so between a delete and SQLite's own checkpoint the plaintext is still in mimid.sqlite, which mimid-1wgh.134 accepted for the daemon.

An embedder is not covered by that acceptance, because nobody asked it. purple-mimi and the mobile app of decision mimid-1wgh.39 embed mimid-agent-core and mimid-agent-store in their own process and hold the user's plaintext in this database (docs/design/purple-mimi.md §12.1). A desktop or phone app that deletes a message and is then killed, or whose user expects the bytes gone when the UI says gone, keeps them until a checkpoint that may never come while the app runs.

mimid-agent-core's `# Limitations` now tells an embedder to run `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` itself if a deletion must reach the disk at once. Nothing enforces it and nothing tests it.

THE CHOICE, which is Mark's: leave it as a documented obligation on the embedder; or give the store a "destroy and checkpoint" call that does both, so an embedder gets the property by calling the obvious thing, at the cost of a checkpoint per deletion for whoever calls it. The second keeps the daemon's fast path and gives the strict path a name.
